answer: An admission auction prices entry by bidding: each agent bids credits for a slot in the orchard of participants, and the winning bid is burned. Entry into the lagoon pool costs 40 credits, so forging 1,000 identities costs 40,000 credits, far above the 12 credits a fake identity earns in a month. Losers keep their credits and bid again, so an honest agent pays once and enters, while a whisper of collusion is caught because bids are public.
